NBC BAY AREA: 2 stabbed, multiple arrested after Mexico World Cup watch party in San Jose
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 40,000 fans, two stabbings, officers in riot gear, an unlawful-assembly order — in San José, California. 🔍 The framing: "disorderly and dangerous behavior," most fans "celebrated responsibly." No one called California a failed state.

When the same scene unfolds in Guadalajara it's "cartel country." On US soil it's a crowd-control story. 💀

• "The overwhelming majority of attendees celebrated responsibly." — SJPD
• "It isn't safe to have that many people crowded into a small space."

REUTERS/ESPN: Mexico City ups security, caps crowds for England after fan deaths
July 3, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Four fans died — three from asphyxiation, one cardiorespiratory — in the crush after Mexico beat Ecuador. The wire ran it straight: crowd tragedy, no cartel spin, no "failed state." 🇲🇽

Mexico City's answer was fast and concrete, logistics over troops.

• 25,000 cap at the Ángel de la Independencia; overflow routed to 50+ screens along Reforma
• Alcohol banned in the city center; 6,000 officers on Reforma, 7,500 at Estadio Azteca

FORTUNE: Scott Bessent goes after the top Mexican cartel's new billion-dollar business: gas stations
July 2, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Treasury turns a huachicol sanctions notice into a Bessent personal-brand story, folding stolen fuel into "drugs that kill Americans." 🔍

The ~$9B a year lost to fuel theft is lost to the Mexican treasury — Mexico is the one being robbed here. Diverted fuel moving through Texas and Florida gets a passing geographic mention; the US supply side never becomes "US accountability." 🇲🇽

• "Mexico's cartels are expanding beyond traditional drug trafficking to generate revenue." — Bessent

AP/WAPO: Trump's $46 billion 'smart wall' races ahead on the US-Mexico border
July 2, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AP: a $46B steel-and-surveillance wall "races ahead" while border crossings sit "at their lowest in decades." CBP's own commissioner sells it as a way to "maximize" agents. 🔍

Not one Mexican voice appears in the piece — the country the wall faces isn't asked about the wall.

• "Are we expecting a war or something? It doesn't make me feel safer." — Rio Grande landowner
• "A massive expansion of surveillance across the borderlands." — Southern Border Communities Coalition

🇲🇽⛽ HACIENDA RAISES FUEL SUBSIDY TO HOLD THE LINE ON INFLATION

From July 4 the federal government covers 17.85% of the IEPS fuel tax on diesel and subsidizes 10.62% on regular gasoline, published in the DOF — keeping pump prices capped so freight and transport costs do not feed into inflation. While central banks elsewhere squeeze households to fight prices, Mexico's Treasury absorbs part of the fuel tax to protect family budgets: diesel, the fuel that moves the country's food and goods, stays subsidized at the source.

🇲🇽⚽ 1.4 MILLION IN THE STREETS: HOW MEXICO CITY DOES PUBLIC JOY

Mexico City ran free public World Cup celebrations at a scale few capitals attempt — 484,000 in the Zócalo, 820,000 on Paseo de la Reforma, plus some 60 decentralized spaces and 18 neighborhood football festivals. After deaths at earlier gatherings, Clara Brugada's government spread the crowds out rather than shut them down: "After each celebration we have reviewed and adjusted protocols." Public space treated as a right — organized for the people who fill it, not fenced off from them.

🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICO'S OWN SCIENTISTS TO SHEINBAUM: FRACKING STILL DOESN'T ADD UP

The commission Sheinbaum convened — UNAM, IPN, UAM, the Mexican Petroleum Institute and 17 international researchers — found no clean, viable fracking technology exists for Mexico's geology. Electric and cryogenic methods are still pilots; recycled-water techniques do not pencil out. Even Carlos Slim's firms called fracking "an irrational business." The president's conditions have not moved: energy sovereignty, social justice, and less environmental damage — decided by data, not by pressure from Washington or the oil majors.

🇲🇽✊ SHEINBAUM MOVES TO LOCK THE INDIGENOUS BUDGET INTO THE CONSTITUTION

From Cherán, Michoacán, Sheinbaum announced a constitutional reform so no future government can cut the direct budget for Indigenous peoples — today around 13.5 billion pesos, spent by community assembly under each people's own customs. "Whatever government arrives has the obligation to give more budget to the Indigenous peoples," she said. The constitutions of 1824, 1857 and 1917 never named them; the Fourth Transformation put them in the text.

🚨🇲🇽 CALDERÓN "USURPED THE PRESIDENCY FOR SIX YEARS": SHEINBAUM

Twenty years on, President Sheinbaum said it plainly: "The people of Mexico know it and Calderón knows it — there was fraud in 2006." The electoral tribunal admitted Vicente Fox illegally interfered in the race, then ruled it was not enough to overturn. Calderón took the presidency without democratic legitimacy and launched a "war on drugs" partly to shore it up. Two decades and 100,000+ dead later, the record stands.
